The Aschenfeld. Grey to the horizon, under a sky the
colour of an old bruise, and in the middle of it the
Host's camp: tents of red hide, engines of timber and
brass, and in the heart of the camp a glow like a
There. The cauldron. Everything that fell today is in
that pot, my Lord. Let's give them back.
A brass patrol, marching in step.
Oni at a fire, sharpening clubs. They look up.
Hellhounds, chained to a post. Not anymore.
The cauldron's guard: an oni captain and his
The cauldron: brass and bone, big as a house, boiling
with something that isn't water. Faces rise to the top
and sink again. It hums a hymn to itself.
Rank D, and made of souls. Light hurts it, my Lord.
The cauldron cracks from rim to foot. Light pours out of
it, hundreds of little lights, and rises into the grey,
Coins. Somebody is dropping coins, one at a time, from
Two hundred and eleven souls, at the market rate. Do
you know what you just cost me, little vessel?
And the General who was refused. How are you, Hanma?
Still angry? I have a contract for anger.
Let us do business, vessel. Sign with me, and your
vessels never run out. Every one of them will be yours
to wake in. Die as often as you like. I only take a
small percentage. On each death. Of your soul.
Ten. Only ten. After ten deaths, of course, there is
nothing left to take, and you are mine.
Let me show you the price of no.
On the ash, the golden chain winds around Hanma's throat,
and Kanta gets up. She doesn't know how.
Cold. A wall of ice as tall as the engines stands between
you and the Brass Tyrant, and on the other side of it a
figure in white walks out of the ash.
…Tsukishiro. The last of the Morgenwacht. You're
No? Never anything, from you. Very well.
Keep your souls, vessel. For now. Everyone signs, in
the end. I am a very patient man.
